name: Andean Gull
rangeDescription: Andean lakes of ecuador to northern argentina and central chile
description: Handsome hooded gull of the Andes; also ranges to coastal areas in nonbreeding season. Found at lakes, wetlands, and bogs; ranging to plowed fields and farmland, and beaches and river mouths on the coast.

name: Comoro Black Parrot
rangeDescription: Comoros (grand comoro and anjouan)
description: Fairly large, black parrot that is found in humid forest, and sometimes in adjacent plantations. Often seen in flight, sometimes in small, loose flocks.

name: Tasmanian Boobook
rangeDescription: Tasmania and islands in bass strait
description: Small brownish owl with dark ‘glasses’ surrounding eyes. Fairly common in a wide variety of habitats on Tasmania.

name: Rufous-winged Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Forest and edge of lowlands and foothills on caribbean slope from eastern guatemala to nicaragua, thence both slopes in costa rica and western panama
description: Fairly small woodpecker, overall olive-green with bright red crown and mustache. Barred belly.

name: Buru Monarch
rangeDescription: Lowlands of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A little-known black-and-white flycatcher-like species restricted to the island of Buru. Has a black hood, a striking white facial mark below the eye, all-black upperparts, and white outer tail feathers, lower chest, and belly.

name: Black Catbird
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern mexico (yucatán peninsula and adjacent islands) to northern honduras
description: Slender-billed, glossy black bird of humid forest, woodland, thickets, and overgrown clearings; shape and habits like Gray Catbird of North America. Common on Cozumel Island, but generally uncommon to rare on the Yucatan mainland.

name: Black-tailed Oriole
rangeDescription: Eastern african and albertine rift montane forest
description: Old World oriole with mostly yellow plumage, a black hood, and a red bill. Found in montane forest.

name: Purple-crowned Fairy
rangeDescription: Gulf slope of southeastern mexico to southwestern ecuador (el oro)
description: Flashy, rather large hummingbird of humid tropical lowlands. Favors forest edges, adjacent clearings with scattered trees and flowering bushes, and gardens.

name: Gray-winged Inca-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of northern peru (central marañón valley, and very local on west slope of andes in cajamarca)
description: Gray finch-like bird known from only a few sites in the Andes of northern Peru, including steep slopes above the Marañon Valley. Adult has bright yellow bill and legs, black mask, and white outer tail feathers that are hard to see when perched.

name: White-edged Oriole
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of western ecuador and northwestern peru (southward to la libertad)
description: Bright orange-and-black bird found in dry forest in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru. The only other oriole in its range is Yellow-tailed Oriole; White-edged lacks yellow on the underside of the tail, has more extensive white in the wing, and is usually (but not always) a deeper orange color.

name: Bougainville Hooded Whistler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of bougainville (northwestern solomon islands)
description: A distinctive whistler of dark, dingy appearance. Golden-olive above and bright yellow below, with a black hood and chest.

name: Dickcissel
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern north america; winters to southern mexico to northern south america
description: Sparrowlike bird known for gathering in enormous wintering flocks in South America. Males are striking with yellow breast, black patch on throat, and rufous shoulders.

name: James's Flamingo
rangeDescription: High andes of southern peru to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Rather local; found at salt lakes and bogs in the high Andes. Associates readily with Chilean and Andean Flamingos, although each species often stays slightly apart within mixed groups.

name: Malaysian Blue Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southern thai-malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Small flycatcher with brilliant blue upperparts, a pale orange throat and chest, and a white belly. Slightly paler female has a whitish throat, while male’s is blue; sexes are otherwise quite similar.

name: Band-tailed Antshrike
rangeDescription: Suriname, french guiana, and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: A rarely encountered large antshrike. Both sexes are distinctive; male is mostly black with a broad white tail band, whereas female is mostly rusty-colored with a black face and throat.

name: Long-billed Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Eastern himalayas (sikkim to eastern assam and northeastern myanmar)
description: Streaky, short-tailed brown bird with a long, slightly decurved bill; the only wren-babbler in its range to have a long bill. Long pale streaks all over the body give it a slick-feathered appearance.

name: Sick's Swift
rangeDescription: Breeds from eastern bolivia southward to northern argentina and eastward to east-central brazil; partially migratory, wintering north to panama, northern colombia, northern venezuela, and suriname
description: Small swift with a uniform brown body contrasting with a pale-ochre rump and slightly paler throat. The tail is square-tipped and quite short.

name: Orinoco Piculet
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia, adjacent southern venezuela (southern amazonas), and northwestern brazil
description: This scarce piculet is known only from a few locations in the humid lowlands of eastern Colombia, southern Venezuela, and northwestern Brazil. Its underparts are entirely barred, but upperparts are plain, lacking the barring shown by the otherwise very similar Lafresnaye’s Piculet.

name: Ashy Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off california; ranges to southern baja california
description: Medium-sized, dark-rumped storm-petrel with a long, deeply notched tail and grayish tones to the plumage. Usually flies fairly directly with light fluttering wingbeats; can be stronger in windy conditions.

name: Tawny-collared Nightjar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern mexico (nuevo león to oaxaca and chiapas)
description: Fairly large dark nightjar of woodland, edge, and adjacent clearings in northeast Mexico. Hunts mainly from perches at forest edge, sometimes even on fence posts in rather open areas.
